analysis.evidence: In וַיַהְוֶה אָמַר אֶל אַבְרָם, Yahweh is the speaker and Abram is the addressee. The source gloss identifying the priest of On does not fit this name or context.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to the proper name יַהְוֶה, the subject of אָמַר.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 66321:1, 66320:2, 66307:5, 66305:15.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In אָמַר אֶל אַבְרָם, “said to Abram,” אֶל introduces Abram as the person Yahweh addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: אָמַר אֶל אַבְרָם means “said to Abram.” The phrase identifies Abram as the person Yahweh addresses after Lot parts from him.
analysis.morphology: Personal proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The preposition אֶל is a separate word.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add the sense ‘part company’ to the Niphal of פָּרַד.
draft.definition: To part company with someone by going one's own way.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 13:9 Abram asks Lot to separate from him and offers to go in whichever direction Lot leaves open.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי הִפָּרֶד לוֹט מֵעִמּוֹ means ‘after Lot had parted company with him’. The phrase מֵעִמּוֹ identifies Abram as the person Lot left.
analysis.morphology: Niphal infinitive construct governed by אַחֲרֵי ‘after’. The initial הִ is part of the verbal stem. לוֹט is the subject of the infinitive.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי הִפָּרֶד לוֹט מֵעִמּוֹ means “after Lot had separated from him.” לוֹט names the person who parted from Abram.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. Lot is the subject of the infinitive construct הִפָּרֶד.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הִפָּרֶד לוֹט מֵעִמּוֹ, Lot is the one who separates, and the suffix identifies Abram as the person whose company Lot leaves.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition מֵ־ (from) combines with עִם (with). The third-person masculine singular suffix וֹ refers to Abram.
